parole.significato: Any of several species of fish in the genera Brevoortia and Ethmidium, used for fish meal, fish oil, fertilizer, and ba…
parole.testo: From Narragansett munnawhatteaug (“they fertilize”), influenced by poghaden.

parole.significato: A fish: the scup or porgy.
parole.testo: From the same Narragansett name for the fish (mishcùp) as scuppaug, scup and paugie.

parole.significato: Any member of the species Fundulus heteroclitus of hardy killifishes, found in brackish and coastal waters of the Unite…
A horse of a once-renowned, now-extinct Rhode Island breed of sure-footed, dependable horses.
parole.testo: Named after the town in Rhode Island, named for the Narragansett tribe.
From Narragansett neeshauog (“eels, lampreys”) or a related word.
Borrowed from Narragansett netoup, netop (“my friend, companion”). Compare Abenaki nidôba (“my friend”).

parole.significato: A fish, Stenotomus chrysops, the porgy.
parole.testo: Shortened form of the Narragansett word mishcùppaûog ("porgies", plural). Another shortening of the same word yields the synonym scup. The full word was borrowed as scuppaug. The singular was borrowed as mishcup. Possibly reinforced by its similarity to porgy, especially in non-rhotic accents.
From the latter part of the Narragansett wampumpeag.

parole.significato: A member of a tribe of Native Americans who historically inhabited eastern Connecticut and spoke a variety of Mohegan-P…
parole.testo: Attested in English since the 1620s/1630s, from Narragansett Pequttôog (“people of the shoals”) (compare Abenaki pôgwa (“shallow, shoal”)).
Shortening of the earlier spelling pequaock, from Narragansett poquauhock.

parole.significato: A chief of one or several Native American tribe(s), especially of the Algonquians; a sagamore.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Narragansett sachem; compare Mi'kmaq saqamaw (“chief”) and Unami sakima (“chief”), all ultimately from Proto-Algonquian *sa·kima·wa. Doublet of sagamore.

parole.significato: A common sparoid food fish, Stenotomus chrysops, of temperate regions of the Atlantic coast of North America; the porgy.
parole.testo: Shortened form of Narragansett mishcùp (“porgy”) or its plural mishcùppaûog. The singular was also borrowed as mishcup, while another shortening of the plural yields the synonym paugie. The word was also borrowed as scuppaug.
From the Narragansett term mishcùppaûog, actually a plural, the singular being mishcùp(p), whence mishcup. Compare scup, paugie.
Borrowed from Narragansett *askútasquash, cognate to Unami kèskùnthàkw, Mohegan-Pequot áskot.

parole.significato: A plant and its fruit of any of a few species of the genus Cucurbita, or gourd kind.
parole.testo: Shortening of Narragansett askutasquash (“[a vegetable] eaten green (or raw)”), from askut (“green, raw”) + asquash (“eaten”).

parole.significato: An early onset of winter, an early (October) cold snap, often followed by flurries of snow.
parole.testo: squaw + winter. The Narragansett word squaw was applied by Europeans to a large number of unrelated things; see the Derived terms section of the entry squaw.

parole.significato: A stew made from kernels of corn, lima beans, tomatoes and sometimes peppers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Narragansett msíckquatash (“boiled corn kernels”).

parole.significato: A fish of the wrasse family found in salt water off of eastern North America from Nova Scotia to South Carolina (Tautog…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Narragansett tautauog, plural of taut.
